question: Can complementary majority-level corroboration retain all three local bindings while rejecting both same-scene sibling-door negatives without another model call?

decision_rule.local_requirement: The predecessor bilateral mask-paired binding must commit.
decision_rule.global_corroborator: The target component must have at least 0.5 inliers under the target-excluded full-frame fundamental matrix, inherited unchanged from the frozen global-epipolar result.
decision_rule.active_corroborator: Both reference-to-query branches must pass and at least half of each predicted query mask must form paired coherent cycles to the other query view.
decision_rule.threshold_origin: The value 0.5 is the same majority principle already frozen for component dominance and global epipolar support; no numeric sweep is performed.

forbidden_after_freeze: change the 0.5 majority, Boolean composition, pair, label or inherited decision
re-run, tune or repair either model result
use provider geometry, target identity or query truth in the recomposed binding decision
claim success on this consumed five-pair panel is fresh confirmation or arbitrary sibling-door generalization
claim_boundary: This is a zero-model posthoc Development recomposition of two already consumed five-pair results. It can establish only that complementary global-geometry and active-query majority receipts fit this observed panel better than either hard gate alone. It is not fresh confirmation, provider-independent generalization, raw-camera binding, arbitrary sibling-door rejection, named entrance, ownership, access, traversability, waypoint, arrival, handoff, Android deployment, benefit, reliability or safety evidence.
